stories.headline: Orchestra Bio brings agent coordination to drug programs

read_evidence.scope: Complete acquisition announcement: program-level evidence coordination, study and manufacturing dependencies, timeline effects, response options, human decision ownership, company integration direction, undisclosed transaction terms and absence of independent outcome measurements.

reading_time_evidence.caveat: Approximate publisher reading time; no individual reading session measured.

stories.summary: OpenAI agreed to acquire Orchestra Bio, whose agents coordinate evidence across studies, manufacturing dependencies and drug-program timelines. The system is intended to surface downstream effects and response options while program leaders retain decisions. OpenAI did not disclose transaction terms or independent outcome measurements, so the announcement establishes direction rather than demonstrated benefit.
stories.why_it_matters: Program leaders can evaluate this pattern without coding: choose one disruption, ask for affected studies, milestones and response options, then verify every source and accountable owner. Keep final schedule or manufacturing changes behind named human approval.
stories.related_coverage: Other October 21 stories cover inference operations, orchestration boundaries, workplace context, public-sector review, biopharma coordination and reusable meeting skills.
stories.image_alt_intent: A biopharma program leader reviews a dependency map linking one study disruption to manufacturing milestones, evidence sources, response options and accountable owners.

audience_fit.intended_user: Biopharma program leaders coordinating studies, manufacturing dependencies and partner decisions without writing software.
audience_fit.practical_action: Delegate study monitoring and timeline-impact comparison, then review the gathered evidence and response options in the program workspace.
audience_fit.review_action: Confirm source records, affected milestones and accountable owners before approving any change to a drug-development plan.
audience_fit.usable_outcome: A reviewed impact brief that links one disruption to affected studies, timelines, decisions and named follow-up owners.

stories.headline: Turn meeting review into one reusable Plaud Skill

source.title: Skills: save your workflows for reuse (for v4.0.x or later)

read_evidence.scope: Complete support procedure: saved instruction sets, five creation paths, draft review before save, Work mode and credit requirements, automatic invocation, routine use, 100-skill limit, editing and deletion controls, and workflow-level limitations.

reading_time_evidence.caveat: Approximate publisher reading time; no individual reading session measured.

stories.summary: Plaud’s Skills feature saves reusable instruction sets that can be created from templates, conversations, files, forms or artifacts, then invoked automatically in Work mode. Users review a draft before saving, and the platform limits each workspace to 100 skills. Usage consumes Plaud Credits, so repeatability still needs cost and quality checks.
stories.why_it_matters: Create one meeting-decision skill that extracts decisions, owners, deadlines and open questions with transcript evidence. Test it on three varied recordings, compare every claim with the source, and require human approval before saving the skill or sharing its brief.
stories.related_coverage: Other October 21 stories cover inference operations, orchestration boundaries, workplace context, public-sector review, biopharma coordination and reusable meeting skills.
stories.image_alt_intent: Three meeting transcripts flow through a reusable decision-brief skill into reviewed cards for decisions, owners, deadlines, open questions and traceable evidence.
stories.agent_skills_evidence: Create a reusable `meeting-decision-brief` Skill for recorded discussions. Accept one recording or transcript plus the meeting purpose and participant list. Extract decisions, named owners, stated deadlines and unresolved questions; attach a verbatim evidence pointer to every item; flag uncertainty rather than guessing; and return a structured brief. Review the generated draft before saving. Test three fixtures covering a clear decision, conflicting owner statements and an unstated deadline. The Skill never sends messages, changes calendars or assigns work. A human must compare each item with the source and approve both the saved procedure and every distributed brief.

audience_fit.intended_user: Consultants, project managers and meeting facilitators who repeatedly convert recorded discussions into decision-ready briefs.
audience_fit.practical_action: Create a meeting-decision Skill from a reviewed template that extracts decisions, owners, deadlines and unresolved questions.
audience_fit.review_action: Compare every extracted decision, owner and deadline with the recording or transcript before saving or sharing the brief.
audience_fit.usable_outcome: A consistent decision brief with traceable evidence, explicit open questions and clearly assigned human follow-up.
